scheme_name: Himachal Pradesh Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar (state Sanitation Reward Scheme)
description:
The Himachal Pradesh Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar is a state-level sanitation reward scheme launched by the Government of Himachal Pradesh. 

This scheme was initiated in 2018 to promote cleanliness and sanitation across the state. 

The launch date of the scheme was 2nd October 2018, coinciding with the celebration of Gandhi Jayanti. 

The background of this initiative is rooted in the Swachh Bharat Mission launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

The Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar aims to encourage local bodies and communities to achieve and maintain high standards of sanitation. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to recognize and reward the efforts of urban local bodies in maintaining cleanliness and sanitation. 

The scheme specifically targets urban local bodies including municipal corporations, councils, and nagar panchayats. 

The measurable targets include achieving a significant reduction in open defecation and improving solid waste management practices. 

The scheme aims to enhance public awareness about sanitation and hygiene practices among the citizens of Himachal Pradesh. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial rewards for the best-performing urban local bodies. 

The total prize money allocated for the scheme is ₹1 crore. 

The prize money is distributed among the top-performing urban local bodies based on their performance in sanitation and cleanliness. 

The first prize is ₹50 lakh, the second prize is ₹30 lakh, and the third prize is ₹20 lakh. 

Additionally, there are various categories of awards based on different criteria such as innovation in sanitation practices and community participation. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on urban local bodies in Himachal Pradesh. 

All municipal corporations, councils, and nagar panchayats are eligible to participate in the scheme. 

There are no specific age limits or income criteria as the scheme is directed towards local governance bodies. 

The application process for the scheme involves a detailed assessment of sanitation practices by the respective urban local bodies. 

Each urban local body must submit a report detailing their sanitation initiatives and achievements. 

The required documents include a comprehensive sanitation plan, photographs of sanitation facilities, and community engagement reports. 

The assessment is conducted by a committee formed by the state government. 

The timeline for the application process is typically announced annually. 

The awards are usually announced on 2nd October each year to coincide with the launch date of the scheme. 

The disbursement of prize money occurs shortly after the announcement of the awards. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Urban Development Department of Himachal Pradesh. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Contact details for the Urban Development Department can be found on the official Himachal Pradesh government website. 

The scheme also aims to promote the involvement of citizens in sanitation efforts. 

Community participation is encouraged through awareness campaigns and educational programs. 

The scheme emphasizes the importance of sustainable sanitation practices. 

It aims to foster a sense of responsibility among citizens regarding cleanliness. 

The Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar is part of a broader initiative to improve public health in the state. 

The scheme aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations, particularly Goal 6, which focuses on clean water and sanitation. 

The scheme has seen participation from various urban local bodies since its inception. 

Regular workshops and training sessions are conducted to educate local bodies on best practices in sanitation. 

The state government has also introduced various incentives for local bodies to improve their sanitation infrastructure. 

The scheme has contributed to a noticeable improvement in the sanitation rankings of Himachal Pradesh. 

According to the Swachh Survekshan 2021, several urban local bodies in Himachal Pradesh have improved their rankings significantly. 

The scheme has also led to increased awareness among citizens about the importance of sanitation and hygiene. 

Local bodies are encouraged to innovate and adopt new technologies for waste management. 

The scheme promotes the use of eco-friendly materials and practices in sanitation. 

It also emphasizes the need for regular maintenance of sanitation facilities. 

The Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar has become a benchmark for sanitation initiatives in the state. 

The success of the scheme is measured through various indicators such as the number of public toilets constructed and the reduction in open defecation. 

The scheme has also inspired similar initiatives in other states. 

The government regularly reviews the progress of the scheme and makes necessary adjustments to improve its effectiveness. 

The scheme has been well-received by the public and local bodies alike. 

Feedback from participants is collected to enhance the scheme's future iterations. 

The Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar is a testament to the commitment of the Himachal Pradesh government towards achieving a clean and healthy environment for its citizens. 

The scheme continues to evolve with changing sanitation needs and challenges faced by urban local bodies. 

Overall, the Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar represents a significant step towards improving sanitation and public health in Himachal Pradesh. 

It serves as a model for other states to implement similar sanitation initiatives. 

The scheme not only rewards performance but also fosters a culture of cleanliness and responsibility among citizens. 

Through this initiative, the Himachal Pradesh government aims to create a cleaner and healthier future for all its residents.
